holidays.name: National Gumdrop Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the chewy, sugar-coated little candies that come in every color of the rainbow. Bite into a gumdrop and let the sweet, squishy joy commence!
holidays.origin: Gumdrops date back to the 1800s, when candymakers began using starch molds to shape fruit-flavored gelled candies coated in sugar. The day is an unofficial food observance that grew out of candy-themed calendar listings.
holidays.funFact: Gumdrops are often not made with actual gum. Early versions did use gum arabic, which is how the candy got its name, and many modern versions use pectin or starch instead.

holidays.name: Singles Awareness Day
holidays.description: The unofficial sequel to Valentine's Day, held for people who are single, or anyone who wants to celebrate friends, family, and self-love. It is also the day to snag heavily discounted chocolate.
holidays.origin: The tongue-in-cheek holiday emerged in the early 2000s, with the acronym S.A.D. playing on the mood some people feel around Valentine's Day. Over time it has been embraced as a day of self-care and Galentine's-style gatherings.
holidays.funFact: Retailers slash prices on Valentine's candy and cards on February 15, which makes it one of the best days of the year to stock up on discounted chocolate.

holidays.name: Susan B. Anthony Day
holidays.description: A day honoring the American suffragist and women's rights activist who campaigned tirelessly for the right to vote. It is celebrated with history lessons, voting-rights events, and visits to her grave, which supporters often decorate with 'I Voted' stickers.
holidays.origin: Susan B. Anthony was born on February 15, 1820, in Adams, Massachusetts. The day has been recognized as a commemorative observance in several states, including Florida, Wisconsin, and West Virginia.
holidays.funFact: In 1872 Anthony was arrested for voting illegally in a presidential election. She was fined $100 and never paid a cent of it.

holidays.name: National Wisconsin Day
holidays.description: Cheese curds, brats, and Packers pride. This day is for celebrating the Badger State and all of its dairy-fueled glory.
holidays.origin: The observance is usually tied to Wisconsin's cultural identity, and it fits into the broader trend of unofficial state-pride days that circulate through social media and local tourism boards.
holidays.funFact: Wisconsin produces over 3 billion pounds of cheese a year, and residents are nicknamed 'Cheeseheads' after the foam cheese hats worn by sports fans.

holidays.name: Global Movie Day
holidays.description: A worldwide celebration of cinema, where fans are encouraged to watch a favorite film, host a screening, and share their love for movies on social media.
holidays.origin: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences launched Global Movie Day in 2006 as a way to encourage people everywhere to enjoy films together. It is now held on the third Saturday in February, so its date shifts annually, and it sometimes falls on the 15th.
holidays.funFact: Libraries, theaters, schools, and even hospitals around the world have held Global Movie Day screenings, with events reported on every continent.
